types.name: Simple present
types.description: The given sentence is in simple present: active uses V1 or V1+s/es (do/does in negatives and questions) and passive uses is/am/are + past participle, e.g. 'The gardener waters the plants' or 'English is spoken here'.

types.name: Simple past
types.description: The given sentence is in simple past: active uses the past form V2 (did in negatives) and passive uses was/were + past participle, e.g. 'Marvel Comics created Superman' or 'The match was won by our team'.

types.name: Future tenses
types.description: The given sentence uses will/shall: simple future (will + V1 / will be + V3) or future perfect (will have + V3 / will have been + V3), e.g. 'They will announce the results tomorrow'.

types.name: Present continuous
types.description: The given sentence uses is/am/are + -ing in active, or is/am/are being + past participle in passive, e.g. 'The workers are repairing the bridge'.

types.name: Past continuous
types.description: The given sentence uses was/were + -ing in active, or was/were being + past participle in passive, e.g. 'She was cooking dinner'.

types.name: Present perfect
types.description: The given sentence uses has/have + past participle in active, or has/have been + past participle in passive, e.g. 'They have completed the building'.

types.name: Past perfect
types.description: The given sentence uses had + past participle in active, or had been + past participle in passive, e.g. 'The sailors had never encountered such a rough sea'.

types.name: Modal verbs
types.description: The verb phrase has a modal such as can, could, may, might, must, should, would, ought to, has to or is to, with passive form modal + be + past participle, e.g. 'We can buy books online' or 'My request should be considered'.

types.name: Verbs with two objects
types.description: The verb takes two objects, a person and a thing (give, send, offer, teach, show, tell, lend, award, ask), so the passive can start with either object, e.g. 'She gave me a pen'.

types.name: Commands and requests
types.description: The given sentence is an order, request, advice or prohibition that starts with a verb or with please/do not/let, and the passive uses 'Let ... be + past participle' or 'You are requested/advised/ordered to', e.g. 'Shut the door'.

types.name: Questions
types.description: The given sentence is a question (yes/no question with do/does/did/is/has/can, or a wh-question with who/what/why/when/where/how), and the answer must stay a question, e.g. 'Who wrote this letter?' or 'Did you hear that noise?'.

types.name: Special structures
types.description: The sentence has a structure beyond a plain tense change: an infinitive or gerund (want someone to do, need to be done), a prepositional or phrasal verb (laugh at, look after), 'It is said / People say that', verbs like know/please/surprise that take with/at/to instead of by, or a negative with nobody/no one.
